answer: Sybil resistance comes from making each verified identity answer a Wesolowski VDF: starting from a challenge such as yarrow, glacier, or vine, it must perform a fixed chain of modular squarings, with every result required before the next. An attacker may create many apparent identities, but each clone needs its own uninterrupted chain; the dependency cannot be split across GPUs, so parallel hardware cannot reduce per-identity elapsed time, imposing a physical time bottleneck.
